# n-seo (En Dash SEO)

> n-seo (full name: En Dash SEO) is an open-source, self-hosted, agentic SEO / AEO / GEO control plane from En Dash Consulting. It pulls Google Search Console and GA4 into local JSON every morning, probes your live sites for regressions (robots.txt, sitemap, soft 404s, blocked AI crawlers, JS-only shells), and ranks the moves worth making, with the evidence attached. That engine is deterministic code; the judgment is handed to an LLM provider the user chooses, and anything that would change a site is handed to the user. It briefs and proposes; it never posts, publishes, or edits.

- Repository: https://github.com/en-dash-consulting/n-seo
- License: MIT
- Requirements: Node 20+, Python 3.10+, curl; macOS, Linux or Windows
- Standalone project: n-seo is NOT installed inside a website's codebase. `n-seo init` creates its own directory for the config, the action queue, content drafts and a `data/` tree the daily run rewrites every morning, and it refuses to scaffold into an application directory or a git repository it does not own (`--force` overrides). It reads sites through the Search Console and GA4 APIs, so it never needs to live in their code. One instance watches as many sites as the owner has
- Quickstart: `npm install -g n-seo`, then `n-seo init my-sites && cd my-sites && n-seo demo && n-seo start` (synthetic data, no Google setup), run from anywhere outside your site repos
- Real data: a Google service-account JSON key added as a user on Search Console and GA4; no gcloud needed
- Bring your own model: the optional `llm` module (off by default) reaches any CLI that reads a prompt on stdin (`claude -p`, `ollama run`, a shell script) or an HTTP endpoint (Anthropic, or anything OpenAI-compatible including gateways and local servers). It writes the opportunity proposals, the verdicts on shipped work, and the community briefings. No API key ships with n-seo. With the module off, the full data-derived queue still works
- Agent access: read-only MCP server (stdio and authenticated HTTP), 16 tools and 3 doc resources, exposing the action queue, per-site metrics, metadata audit, index coverage, trends, and ops status. `.mcp.json` registers it for Claude Code automatically
- Driven by conversation: `n-seo init` installs seven skills into the instance (orient, setup, add-site, triage, ship, review, deploy) plus a `CLAUDE.md` carrying the operating rules, so setup and daily use are things the owner asks for in plain language — "set this up for my sites", "what should I work on today?", "do the first one" — rather than docs to work through. The rules below are enforced by the skills rather than merely documented; the agent can propose and implement but cannot publish, post, or change a site on its own
- Built-in operating rules: 28-day title freeze after any metadata change, at most ~8 metadata changes per week, decisions on the trailing 90 days, impact numbers order the queue and are not forecasts, shipped work is watched rather than deleted, community participation is written by a human
